verses.text: This is the vision Isaiah, Amoz's son, saw about Judah and Jerusalem when Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were kings of Judah.
Heavens, listen up! Earth, pay attention! The LORD has spoken: “I fed my children and raised them, and they turned against me.
An ox knows its owner, and a donkey knows its master's feeding trough. But Israel doesn't know me. My people don't even stop to think.”

What a sinful nation, weighed down with wrongdoing! You're the offspring of evildoers, children who act corruptly. You've walked out on the LORD and treated the Holy One of Israel with contempt. You've turned your backs and gone far away.
Why take another beating just to rebel even more? Your whole head is sick, and your whole heart is weak.
From the bottom of your foot to the top of your head, there's nothing healthy. Just wounds, welts, and open sores. Nobody's closed them up, wrapped them, or soothed them with oil.
Your country is wrecked. Your cities have burned. Strangers are eating up your land right in front of you, leaving it ruined like land taken over by outsiders.
Daughter Zion is left standing like a shelter in a vineyard, like a hut in a melon field, like a city under siege.
If the LORD of Armies hadn't left a tiny group of us alive, we'd have ended up like Sodom. We'd have been just like Gomorrah.
Listen to the LORD's word, you rulers of Sodom! Hear what our God teaches, you people of Gomorrah!
“What do I want with all these sacrifices?” says the LORD. “I've had enough of rams burned as offerings and the fat of well-fed animals. The blood of bulls, lambs, and male goats doesn't please me.
When you show up in front of me, who asked you to come stomping through my courts?
Quit bringing offerings that mean nothing. Your incense disgusts me. Your New Moons, Sabbaths, and gatherings are more than I can stand when there's evil in the assembly.
I hate your New Moons and your scheduled feasts with my whole soul. They're a load on me, and I'm tired of carrying it.
When you spread your hands out, I'll look away. Pray all you want. I won't listen. Your hands are covered in blood.
Wash up. Get clean. Get the evil you're doing out of my sight. Stop doing wrong.
Learn to do good. Go after justice. Help the people being oppressed. Defend children without fathers. Speak up for widows.”
“Come on, let's talk this through,” says the LORD. “Even if your sins are scarlet, they'll be white like snow. Even if they're red like crimson, they'll be like wool.
If you're willing to listen and obey, you'll eat the good things this land grows.
If you refuse and rebel, the sword will devour you.” The LORD himself has spoken.
How did the faithful city become a prostitute? It used to be full of justice. People did what was right there. Now murderers live there.
Your silver has turned to waste metal. Your wine is watered down.
Your rulers are rebels who run with thieves. Every one of them loves a bribe and chases payouts. They don't defend children without fathers, and a widow's case never even gets heard.
So the Lord, GOD of Armies, the Mighty One of Israel, says, “I'll get relief from those who oppose me and take vengeance on my enemies.
I'll turn my hand against you, clean out all your waste metal, and take away all your tin.
I'll bring back your judges like you had at first and your advisers like you had at the beginning. After that, people will call you ‘the city that does right, the faithful town.’
Zion will be bought back through justice, and the people who turn back to her through righteousness.
But rebels and sinners will fall together. The people who walk away from the LORD will be consumed.
You'll be ashamed of the oaks you wanted so badly, and humiliated over the gardens you chose.
You'll be like an oak with leaves that wither, like a garden without water.
The strong will be like dry tinder, and what they've done will be the spark. They'll both burn together, and nobody will put it out.”
